strengths: TRGC2 is a decisive gamma-delta TCR lineage marker and ranks near the top of the DEG list.
T-lineage markers CD3D, CD2, FYN and lower-rank TRAC confirm T-cell identity.
Cytotoxic effector markers GZMK, GZMH, GZMA, GZMB, GZMM, NKG7, CTSW, FGFBP2 and GNLY fit an effector/memory gamma-delta T-cell phenotype.
CD8A/CD8B and NK-like receptors (KLRK1, KLRD1, KLRB1, HCST) are plausibly interpreted within a CD8+ or innate-like gamma-delta T-cell context.
weaknesses: The specific Vdelta2/Vgamma9Vdelta2 subtype inference is not directly supported by TRGV9/TRDV2 markers.
The distinction between CD8+ gamma-delta and CD8+ alpha-beta T cells cannot be fully resolved from the provided markers, but TRGC2 strongly favors gamma-delta.

strengths: Broad T-cell identity is directly supported by CD3D, CD2, FYN and TRAC.
The label is safe and not contradicted by the observed lineage markers.
weaknesses: Under-specified: it does not use TRGC2 to resolve the gamma-delta versus alpha-beta T-cell branch.
The rank-2 subtype CD8-positive alpha-beta T cell lacks direct alpha-beta TCR evidence (e.g., TRBC1/TRBC2, high TRAC) and is not favored over gamma-delta T cell given TRGC2.

Mapping status is review/unmapped and the proposed CLID is not directly supported by the observed branch-specific markers.

supporting: TRGC2 (top DEG) is direct positive evidence for the gamma-delta TCR, supporting hierarchical refinement from T cell to gamma-delta T cell.
CD3D, CD2, FYN and TRAC confirm T-cell lineage.
GZMK, GZMH, GZMA, GZMB, GZMM, NKG7, CTSW, FGFBP2 and GNLY support a cytotoxic effector/memory phenotype consistent with gamma-delta T cells.
CD8A and CD8B are compatible with a CD8+ gamma-delta T-cell subset and do not establish alpha-beta TCR identity.
KLRK1, KLRD1, KLRB1 and HCST reflect the innate-like/NK-like receptor program commonly present in gamma-delta T cells.
Retrieved literature PMIDs 38177168, 38678059, 33932031, 24293448, 27589570, 34124223, 35646049 and 40221598 provide contextual support for gamma-delta T-cell identity.
conflicting: No high-confidence alpha-beta TCR genes (e.g., TRBC1/TRBC2 or strongly elevated TRAC) support a CD8+ alpha-beta T-cell call
